entities.name: CLI
entities.rationale: Developer using the Atlassian Forge CLI to write and deploy custom code.

entities.name: EC2 (Deployment API)
entities.rationale: Ingestion web service on EC2 behind an ALB that receives deployment requests from the CLI.

entities.name: DynamoDB
entities.rationale: Stores the deployment state and progress to report back to the user.

entities.name: SQS
entities.rationale: Queues deployment requests to decouple ingestion and avoid rate limiting Lambda creation.

entities.name: EC2 (Deployment Worker)
entities.rationale: Backend service on EC2 that reads deployment requests from SQS and creates Lambda functions.

entities.name: Browser
entities.rationale: End users accessing Atlassian products via a browser to render page fragments.

entities.name: EC2 (Internal Service)
entities.rationale: Internal service that handles authentication, finds the appropriate customer Lambda, and passes invocation parameters.

entities.name: Lambda
entities.rationale: Multi-tenant Lambda running customer code isolated inside V8 isolates in a separate dedicated customer account.

visual_connections.description: CLI deploys application code to the ingestion EC2 service.
Deployment service records and updates deployment state in DynamoDB.
Deployment service pushes deployment requests onto the SQS queue.
Deployment worker polls and reads deployment requests from the SQS queue.
Worker creates the Lambda function across the account boundary in the customer account.
Browser sends invocation and data requests to the internal EC2 service.
Internal service invokes the target Lambda function across the account boundary.
